name: Marie Reed Haug
bio: Marie Reed Haug was a Cleveland union business representative and Progressive Party committeewoman, one of eight people indicted in January 1957 in a novel Taft-Hartley 'conspiracy' prosecution — charged both with falsely signing the non-Communist affidavit and with conspiring with Communist leaders to obtain NLRB services. The 'conspiracy' theory was the government's attempt to evade the Supreme Court's rejection of ordinary affidavit prosecutions.
charges: Conspiracy to defraud the U.S. via false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits; false affidavit
sentence: Faced up to five years and a $10,000 fine

name: Fred Haug
bio: Fred Haug was an early CIO organizer and former UE and Mine-Mill official in Cleveland, one of the eight indicted in the 1957 Cleveland Taft-Hartley 'conspiracy' case and one of only two charged with personally filing a false non-Communist affidavit. He was the husband of co-defendant Marie Reed Haug.
charges: Conspiracy to defraud the U.S. via false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits; false affidavit
sentence: Faced up to five years and a $10,000 fine

name: Eric Reinthaler
bio: Eric Reinthaler was a former officer of United Electrical Workers Local 735 in Cleveland, indicted in January 1957 in the Taft-Hartley 'conspiracy' case in which the union's civil-rights, peace, and independent-political activity was cited as 'proof' of conspiracy. He engaged his own counsel with the Haugs.
charges: Conspiracy to defraud the U.S. via false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
sentence: Faced up to five years and a $10,000 fine

name: Edward Chaka
bio: Edward Joseph Chaka was one of the eight Cleveland defendants in the 1957 Taft-Hartley 'conspiracy' indictment, alleged to have acted as a 'secret courier' maintaining communication among Communists who filed non-Communist affidavits.
charges: Conspiracy to defraud the U.S. via false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
sentence: Faced up to five years and a $10,000 fine

name: Hyman Lumer
bio: Hyman Lumer was a Cleveland Communist and economist, one of the eight indicted in the 1957 Cleveland Taft-Hartley 'conspiracy' case, alleged to have issued Communist Party instructions to the Haugs. He later became a national party education director and editor.
charges: Conspiracy to defraud the U.S. via false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
sentence: Faced up to five years and a $10,000 fine

name: James West
bio: James West was a Communist Party figure named in the 1957 Cleveland Taft-Hartley 'conspiracy' indictment as having issued a party directive and appointed a 'secret courier' in the alleged scheme. He was one of the eight defendants.
charges: Conspiracy to defraud the U.S. via false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
sentence: Faced up to five years and a $10,000 fine

name: Sam Reed
bio: Sam Reed was one of the eight defendants — several of them from out of state — indicted in the 1957 Cleveland Taft-Hartley 'conspiracy' case built on the theory that union officials had conspired with Communist leaders over their non-Communist affidavits.
charges: Conspiracy to defraud the U.S. via false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
sentence: Faced up to five years and a $10,000 fine

name: Andrew Remes
bio: Andrew Remes was one of the eight defendants indicted in the 1957 Cleveland Taft-Hartley 'conspiracy' case, a prosecution the labor movement attacked as an attempt to revive Taft-Hartley affidavit charges that the courts had been throwing out.
charges: Conspiracy to defraud the U.S. via false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
sentence: Faced up to five years and a $10,000 fine
